To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
changes in the trans-membrane domain of SIV Vpus are sufficient for the acquisition of anti-tethering activity.
The transmembrane domain is sufficient for the acquisition of anti-tethering activity to SIV Vpu proteins from chimpanzees and gorillas.
the transmembrane domains of SIV Vpus are sufficient for tetherin antagonists, and that cytoplasmic motifs of Vpu are dispensable for tetherin antagonization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which Vpu proteins of HIV-1 and related viruses interact with host proteins in the context of HIV-1 pathogenesis and transmission.
a better understanding of the evolution of Vpu proteins in the course of SIVcpzs and SIVgor transmission to humans.
the question of how the HIV-1 VPU gene product counteracts the antiviral protein BST2/Tetherin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TMD of Vpu is sufficient for tetherin antagonistic function and that the cytoplasmatic domains of Vpu are required for other Vpr functions.

Vpu is an extremely complex and multifunctional protein, which is able to perform a number of functions in a cell-type specific manner and that the TMD of the protein is the key determinant of its anti-tetherin functionality.
the TMD of Vpu is the most important domain in Vpu for its function against tetherin, but the cytoplasmatic domains may also contribute to this activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SIVcpz, SIVgor and HIV-1 Vpus are all capable of counteracting the anti-viral activity of tetherin, although some of these Vpu proteins may require additional changes in their cytoplasmic tail to acquire optimal anti-tetherin potency.
the TMD of Vpu is the most crucial determinant for the anti-tetherin effect.
the TMD of HIV-1 Vpu is sufficient to render SIVcpz Vpu proteins active against human tethering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoplasm of Vpu may be a key region for Vpu function.
the TMD of Vpu is the key domain in determining its tetherin antagonism.
the cytoplasm of Vpu is a complex region that may be involved in several functions, including the interaction with tetherin and CD4.
